title: Matrix multiplication with exponent at most 9/4
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that the exponent of matrix multiplication satisfies omega <= 9/4: two n x n complex matrices can be multiplied with O(n^(9/4+eps)) arithmetic operations for every eps > 0. Tensors, restriction, rank and flattening ranks; Strassen's characters (additive, multiplicative, monotone invariants of tensors) and their monotonicity under degenerations; a Fourier separation of blocks sharing one leg and the resulting entropy inequality; a symmetrized profile of the polynomial multiplication tensors, which is discretely concave (a determinant filtration) and satisfies shifted tripling (three sectors); diagonal growth P(a,a) >= a^(4/3), hence lambda(T_d) <= d^(9/4) for every character; existence of characters that are large on matrix multiplication, by a separation argument, a catalytic comparison and Schauder's fixed-point theorem.
prerequisites: linear algebra over a field: bases, matrices of bilinear maps, rank, row reduction, Vandermonde matrices (core course Linear Algebra)

metric spaces, compactness and sequences; Schauder's fixed-point theorem for compact convex subsets of normed spaces, Theorem 5.1 of the lesson Ultrapowers and Darbo's fixed-point theorem (course Tingley's problem)

checks.reading: The manuscript 'An upper bound of 9/4 for the matrix multiplication exponent' (OpenAI, 2 Oct 2026; build/paper.tex, 44 kB; local library copy openai-math-20261006) was read in full on 17 Oct 2026, and every step was derived again while the lessons were written. No error was found. Changes of form in the course: the base field is the countable field F generated by the roots of unity instead of C, so that the state space is a compact convex subset of a normed space (weighted norm, Lemma 6.3) and Schauder's theorem for normed spaces (programme provider) replaces the Schauder-Tychonoff theorem; the conclusion holds over every field containing F, with algorithm constants in F; tensors of bilinear maps and changes of bases are treated explicitly (Lemma 1.3), which makes the dual output leg in the determinant filtration precise; the exact sequence and basis of Lemma 4.2, the type bound for multinomial coefficients (Lemma 3.3), the closedness and separation of finitely generated cones (Lemma 6.5) and rational solutions of rational systems (Lemma 6.6) are proved in the lessons; the separation of Proposition 3.2 is shown to work for every L > 3(M-1), and to fail for L = 3, M = 2 (Exercise 3.4); a linear-programming computation shows that for a <= 16 the bound of Step 3 of Lemma 5.1 is the least value of P(a,a) compatible with its hypotheses on the pairs a, b <= 64. Field state on 17 Oct 2026: no published refutation or peer-reviewed confirmation was found; OpenAI's repository has a Lean entry for family 107 (lean/docs/107.md), and community projects on GitHub report Lean formalizations extending the argument to every field and a note that the 9/4 argument is tight; these were not read in detail.

open_obligations: OpenAI's companion manuscripts of family 107 ('Complex matrix multiplication below 2.258 and rectangular bounds' and 'Staggered extraction for exact matrix multiplication over every field', both 24 Sep 2026) are not treated; the first and last lessons mention them.
The OpenAI repository has a Lean entry for family 107 (lean/docs/107.md); it and the Lean files were not read, and the course does not depend on them.
The optimality remark after Theorem 5.2 rests on a numerical linear-programming computation on a finite range; it is labelled as numerical and is not used in any proof.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
